title: Error-detecting solid codes
summary: A code is called solid if, roughly speaking, any correctly-transmitted codeword in an arbitrarily corrupted string of codewords can still be decoded correctly and unambiguously. So-called variable-length solid codes, in which codewords may differ in length, have been studied by various authors. In this short note, we observe that a recent construction of variable-length solid codes based on binary codes may be extended to arbitrary n-ary codes.
